title: Reconnect a roller blind’s beaded chain
instruction: Reconnect the two ends of the chain through the coupler. Use opposite sides of the closed loop to lower the blind, then raise it back.
context: A clasp can look joined while slipping under load. Cycling the shade checks retention through both sides of the loop.
setup: A tabletop stand holds a 198 mm wide linen-like shade on a 64 mm diameter roll with its axle 443 mm above the simulation origin. A 196 mm aluminium hem bar starts 133 mm below the axle. Two steel uprights and an aluminium headrail support the roll. The side clutch has a 64 mm pitch diameter. Its pre-routed ball chain has approximately 8.4 mm pitch. The clasp rests in a plastic jig at (124, −103, 241) mm and the loose end starts 24 mm farther out along negative y. The 380 × 400 mm mat supports the fixture. The shade starts raised and the chain ends disconnected.
scoring: 0.00 until the terminal passes 23 mm through the clasp and remains beyond 22 mm insertion. Award 1/3 for retaining the join. Award 2/3 when the repaired lowering side also moves the hem more than 22 mm below the raised reference. Award 1.00 when pulling the opposite side raises the hem more than 18 mm from that deepest position to less than 12 mm below the raised reference. Both hands must release the fixture and the join must hold.
reset_notes: Return the hem to the raised mark, disconnect the loose end, place both ends on the jig marks and leave the chain pre-routed over the clutch.
fidelity: The simulation models the clasp retention and two working chain runs as guided contacts. A compliant transmission drives the roller and fabric payout. The bead positions along the inextensible rendered loop are driven by this mechanism.
